slices.note: Face on the left, back of the head on the right.
pts: Biggest bundle of fibres joining the left and right hemispheres.
CSF-filled cavity; CSF is made by the choroid plexus inside it.
Relay station: almost every sense (except smell) passes through it to the cortex.
Master hormone gland sitting in the sella turcica; tumours here press on the optic chiasm.
Top of the brainstem: CN III and IV nuclei, substantia nigra (dopamine, lost in Parkinson's).
Middle of the brainstem: CN V–VIII nuclei and the big bridge of fibres to the cerebellum.
Bottom of the brainstem: breathing and heart-rate centres, the pyramids where motor fibres cross.
Carries motor and sensory tracts; in adults it ends around L1–L2.
Coordination, balance and smooth movement; each side controls the same side of the body.
CSF space between the pons/medulla and the cerebellum; blockage here causes hydrocephalus.
Planning, personality, movement (motor cortex) and, on the dominant side, speech production (Broca).
Touch and body position (sensory cortex), attention to space; damage on the right causes neglect.

slices.note: Seen from the feet: the patient's right is on YOUR left. Front of the head at the top.
pts: Front part of the lateral ventricle, bordered by the caudate head.
Part of the basal ganglia (striatum); shrinks in Huntington's disease, so the horns look boxy.
Basal ganglia (striatum); gets dopamine from the substantia nigra. Common site of hypertensive bleeds.
Motor and sensory fibres squeezed between the basal ganglia and thalamus; a tiny stroke here weakens a whole side.
Relay station: almost every sense (except smell) passes through it to the cortex.
Where the body, occipital and temporal horns meet; the choroid plexus is often calcified here.
Thin membrane separating the two frontal horns.
Planning, personality, movement (motor cortex) and, on the dominant side, speech production (Broca).
Hearing, memory (hippocampus) and, on the dominant side, language understanding (Wernicke).
Deep groove separating frontal and temporal lobes; the insula hides at its bottom; MCA branches run here.

slices.note: Seen from the front: the patient's right is on YOUR left.
pts: CSF-filled cavity; CSF is made by the choroid plexus inside it.
Biggest bundle of fibres joining the left and right hemispheres.
Relay station: almost every sense (except smell) passes through it to the cortex.
Seahorse-shaped memory structure in the temporal lobe; shrinks early in Alzheimer's.
Top of the brainstem: CN III and IV nuclei, substantia nigra (dopamine, lost in Parkinson's).
Middle of the brainstem: CN V–VIII nuclei and the big bridge of fibres to the cerebellum.
Bottom of the brainstem: breathing and heart-rate centres, the pyramids where motor fibres cross.
Hidden lobe deep in the Sylvian fissure: taste, gut feelings, awareness of body state.
Hearing, memory (hippocampus) and, on the dominant side, language understanding (Wernicke).
Midline gap between the hemispheres; the falx cerebri and anterior cerebral arteries sit in it.
Myelinated axons (dark on T2, bright on T1); multiple sclerosis plaques show up here.
